newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU reaches deal on defence in treaty talks.
newsitem.headline: EU reaches deal on defence in treaty talks.

text.p: European Union leaders reached a deal on defence policy at the EU summit in Amsterdam on Tuesday, postponing the question of whether the Western European Union (WEU) should be brought into the bloc.

British Prime Minister Tony Blair and leaders of the bloc's neutral countries had earlier vetoed any firm language calling for the EU to take over a defence role through the WEU, which comprises 10 EU countries.

After hours of negotiation, the EU leaders agreed to add into a new treaty a call for the 15-nation bloc to develop closer relations with the WEU, but with an eye only to the "possibility" of an eventual merger.
Most of the bloc -- led by France and Germany -- had wanted to bring the WEU fully into the Union in order to develop a European defence architecture alongside the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
But Britain -- supported for different reasons by Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Austria and Ireland -- had argued against the move, seeing it as undermining NATO's position.
"It (the agreement) makes it very clear that our defence interests will continue to be looked at in NATO," British Prime Minister Tony Blair said.

The United States and other NATO countries have agreed in principle to lend materiel to the WEU for future peacekeeping and humanitarian aid missions in which the Alliance itself does not wish to participate.
